rules.citation: General Law - Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 11
rules.title: Determination of lease for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent under a written lease, a landlord may terminate the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant can avoid termination in the possession action by paying or tendering all rent then due, with interest and court costs, on or before the day the answer is due.
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit; cure by answer due by paying all rent due with interest and costs

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies where rent is due under a written lease and the tenant neglects or refuses to pay.
coverage.summary: Covers tenants with written leases who have neglected or refused to pay rent due.

rules.exemptions: If nonpayment was caused by failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth, a municipality, or their departments, agencies, or authorities in mailing or delivering a subsistence or rental payment, check, or voucher other than salary, the court must continue the hearing at least seven days and treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent due with interest and costs is tendered within that time.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
